Instead, you're building a chain, a connection between existing behaviors. Habit stacking isn’t about adding a new habit; it’s about linking an old one to a new one. It’s a grammatical structure that makes it incredibly sticky, because it’s anchored in your existing routine.

You’re not stacking “after I brush my teeth, I will floss” just because it sounds good. It needs to be a connection that feels natural, even slightly pleasurable. As you sip your coffee, the thought “After I finish my coffee, I will write one sentence” gently nudges you forward.

The goal isn’t to be impressive; it’s not to maximize output. It’s to create a foothold, a tiny victory that builds momentum. Consider the emotional component too. The new habit shouldn't feel like a chore. If possible, choose a habit that has a slight positive feeling associated with it.  Stacking something you genuinely enjoy, even in a small way, will significantly increase your chances of long-term adherence.
